title: PostGIS Geospatial Engine
description: Store coordinates, compute distances with ST_Distance, find nearest points with GiST index KNN, and handle geometries.

data.text: **PostGIS** is the world's most powerful open-source spatial database engine. It extends PostgreSQL with spatial data types (`GEOMETRY`, `GEOGRAPHY`), spatial indexing (R-Tree over GiST), and hundreds of geospatial functions.

data.title: Finding Drivers Within 5km with PostGIS Geography
data.content: Computes true spheroidal distance in meters using ST_DWithin.

data.text: PostGIS stores geometry in a bounding-box tree (a GiST index), so a spatial query first filters by bounding box and then does the precise distance check. `GEOGRAPHY` computes distance on the sphere in meters, while `GEOMETRY` works in a flat projected plane. Use `ST_DWithin` for radius searches because it is index-aware; `ST_Distance` in a `WHERE` clause computes the distance for every row and cannot use the index.

data.title: Index a location column and find nearby points
data.content: The GiST index accelerates the bounding-box filter; ST_DWithin then applies the true distance and keeps the query sargable.

data.title: Match the type to the question
data.text: Use `GEOGRAPHY` when you need distances in meters between GPS coordinates anywhere on Earth, accepting a modest performance cost. Use `GEOMETRY` with a projected spatial reference system when you need high-performance analysis within a region and are working in a flat plane. Both use a GiST index, but only `GEOGRAPHY` gives you correct spheroidal distances without extra work.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `PostGIS` adds native geospatial support to PostgreSQL.
Use `GEOGRAPHY` for real-world latitude/longitude (GPS) distance calculations in meters.
Use `ST_DWithin` with GiST indexes for sub-millisecond proximity queries.
